source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ας Απριλίου — «Άγιος Πλάτων ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Μπάνια Λούκα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page is a full and dated life: born 29 September 1874 at Belgrade to Ilija Jovanović and Jelka Sokolović; a monk, then deacon and priest; sent in 1896 to the theological academy of Moscow and back in 1901 as superior of the monastery of Rakovica and a teacher; a military chaplain in the First World War and afterwards a carer for orphans and the wounded; elected bishop of Ohrid in 1938 and moved in 1939 to Banja Luka in northern Bosnia; refusing in 1941 to leave his flock when the pro-Nazi Croatian government demanded that the Orthodox Serbs convert or go; seized by the Ustaše with the priest Dušan Subotić and executed, his body thrown into the river Vrbanja and recovered a few days later by Christians of the village of Kumsale, who buried it in the military cemetery of Banja Luka; his relics translated in 1973 to the cathedral of Banja Luka; and his canonisation by the Holy Synod of the Church of Serbia in 1998. **The Serbian row here is still `undocumented`**, although the page names the Serbian synod as the body that canonised him: the row records what was read, and pravoslavno.rs was not read. The corpus keeps several saints named Plato or Platon — of Ancyra, of Megara, the venerable, Aivazidis and Kulbusch — and none of them is this bishop. It prints no hymn.
